targets.behavior_under_test: parseHumanSize() uses DECIMAL SI multipliers: 1e6 for MB, 1e9 for GB. TestParseHumanSize asserts '1.5GB' → 1500000000. TestSearch_ParsesFixture asserts '113.89MB' → 113890000 (fixture only exercises MB).

mutation.description: Change GB multiplier from 1e9 (decimal SI) to 1<<30 (IEC binary GiB) in sizeUnits slice — a FRESH mutation NOT in the existing KDoc rehearsals

targets.observed_failure:
=== RUN TestSearch_ParsesFixture --- PASS: TestSearch_ParsesFixture (0.00s) === RUN TestParseHumanSize tokyotosho_test.go:181: parseHumanSize("Size: 1.5GB
") = 1610612736, want 1500000000 --- FAIL: TestParseHumanSize (0.00s) FAIL FAIL digital.vasic.lava.apigo/internal/provider/curated/tokyotosho 0.244s
targets.verdict: GENUINE — TestParseHumanSize caught the GB multiplier error (1.5 * 1073741824 = 1610612736 vs expected 1500000000)
targets.secondary_finding: TestSearch_ParsesFixture PASSED despite the mutation because the fixture only contains MB-sized rows (113.89MB, 5.93MB); GB entries are absent from the fixture. This is honest — TestSearch_ParsesFixture is fixture-scope complete; TestParseHumanSize provides the GB discriminator via direct unit testing of the parser. No bluff — the combination covers the production path.
targets.note: The 1e9→1<<30 GB mutation is the SI/IEC unit-confusion class. 1 GiB (1073741824) vs 1 GB (1e9) is a ~7% overcount — would silently corrupt the 'size' column for large torrents (films etc.).
